answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake if a randomly selected, independently verifiable task exposes duplicate identities or fabricated results. A sybil attacker must fund every persona separately and risks losing capital on each caught account, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free. For example, an opal-market agent might validate a gale forecast against public sensor records; a marble token can serve as the stake, not as proof of identity.
